java.say: Read this line from the inside out. First `new FlatFileQuestionStorage()` makes the real storage. It saves questions as they are, in plain text.
Then `new EncryptingQuestionStorage(...)` builds the proxy and hands it the real storage, which it keeps in its field `real`. Both classes implement the same interface, QuestionStorage.
The program saves a question. The variable `storage` has the type QuestionStorage, so the program cannot see that a proxy stands in front of the real storage.
The proxy gets the call first. It offers the same save() as the real storage, but it does something extra before it passes the call on: it encrypts the text.
"What is polymorphism?" is scrambled to "V2hhdCBpcyBwb2x5bW9ycGhpc20/". (This example uses Base64 as stand-in encryption.)

java.at: public void save(String id, String text) { file.put(id, text); }
java.say: Now the proxy passes the call on to the real storage, with the scrambled text. The real storage saves whatever it gets; it does not know about encryption.
Done. The program, the interface and the real storage did not change. The only new part is the proxy in between, and you can leave it out again.
